security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, TypeScript template literals, normal environment configuration, and expected ChatKit network calls. One semantic issue remains: the MCP guidance places access tokens into model-visible prompt instructions and tool inputs. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: Access tokens are embedded in MCP prompt instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove access tokens from prompts. Use server-side authorization, token binding, or scoped tool sessions outside model-visible context.

remediation.issue: Context examples may send user and page metadata broadly.
remediation.suggestion: Document data minimization. Redact sensitive page fields before adding metadata to chat requests.

semantic_findings.title: Credentials Exposed in MCP Prompt Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The MCP authentication section places access_token in SYSTEM_PROMPT and instructs every MCP tool call to include it. This exposes credentials to model context and tool inputs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The lines explicitly template access_token into prompt instructions. This is a direct credential exposure pattern, not a scanner artifact.

content.value_statement: Teams need secure AI chat that connects UI, auth, backend agents, and context. This skill provides ChatKit patterns for React, Next.js, Python backends, and cookie proxy flows.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to extend ChatKitServer with a custom Python agent response flow.
Configures useChatKit with a custom fetch interceptor for auth and context metadata.
Explains Next.js httpOnly cookie proxy routing for authenticated chat requests.
Covers script loading detection for ChatKit web components in React and Next.js.
Documents database persistence setup and connection pool warmup for ChatKit stores.
Lists tier boundaries for related streaming and widget skills.
limitations: It is a pattern guide, not a complete runnable application.
Examples require adaptation to your auth provider, database, and deployment model.
The MCP credential prompt example should be redesigned before production use.
Advanced widget actions and streaming lifecycle events are delegated to related skills.

output_examples.input: My app uses httpOnly cookies and the browser cannot read the token.
output_examples.output: A Next.js proxy design that reads the cookie server-side, forwards Authorization to ChatKit, and preserves streaming responses.

output_examples.input: My first ChatKit request is slow after deployment.
output_examples.output: A backend persistence checklist that covers database connection warmup, pool health checks, and request path validation.

best_practices: Keep authentication checks on the server and use client checks only for user experience.
Minimize context sent to agents and remove sensitive page data before transmission.
Load ChatKit web components before rendering dependent React components.
anti_patterns: Do not put long-lived access tokens into prompts or model-visible tool instructions.
Do not read private environment variables in browser-side code.
Do not proxy streaming ChatKit responses through JSON-only response helpers.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build ChatKit-based AI chat interfaces with custom backends, authentication, context injection, and Next.js proxy patterns.

faq.question: Does it include a full application?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation patterns and examples that you adapt to your application.

faq.question: Can it support httpOnly cookie authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows a server-side Next.js proxy pattern for reading cookies and forwarding authenticated chat requests.

faq.question: Does it cover database persistence?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes ChatKit store configuration, database URL setup, and connection pool warmup guidance.

faq.question: Is the MCP token prompt pattern safe?
faq.answer: No. The token-in-prompt pattern should be replaced with server-side authorization before production use.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
